surface: Home (index.html — renderHomeStart / renderHomeHero / homeLead / renderUpNext / renderHomeTiles / install nudge; iOS twins in HomeView.swift, HomeLeadCard.swift, ScheduleModels.swift)
note: All eight submitted findings exist verbatim at (or within two lines of) the cited line, none is demo-gated, none is dead code, and none is a small-caps LABEL mistaken for shouting. Seven survive; HOME-8 is DROPPED. Two corrections worth carrying: (1) HOME-8's stated law is false — the "JOIN OR START" tile (10957) goes to switchView('hub'), and for a league-less golfer #view-hub renders #hubLeagueless, which is literally [Start a league] / [I have a league code] (3595–3606), so the label describes its destination honestly. What is true is bigger than the label and shouldn't be fixed by rewording it: a league-less Home offers join/start in three places — the door row (11039–11041), the hero's own CTA on rung 5 ("Start a league", 11386), and that tile. That is an IA call, not a copy edit. (2) HOME-1's and HOME-4's fixes as submitted over-delete; both are corrected in the rewrites below. Also worth recording as good news: the worked example the owner found today is already fixed in this file — the comment at 11312–11319 documents it and the sub-CTA now reads plain "Post a round" (11320).

All 14 submitted findings were checked in source. Every string exists, none is demo-only, none is dead code, none is a code comment. Corrections made: ROOM-2's supporting citations were off by one (#khTee is 13697 not 13698, #statFinal 10691 not 10692, #nextTxt 10777 not 10778); ROOM-3's cited canon line is index.html:19418 not 19403. Everything else landed on the exact line. Verified NOT defects and therefore not reported: (a) the ALL-CAPS in `phaseSub`, `kickoff.count`, `seatFill`, `squadsSub`, `standingsEmpty` and the `PhaseHero` `m:` slot — these render through `.font(CSFont.label).tracking(1.2).textCase(.uppercase)` (LeagueRoomScreen.swift:170) and `.eyebrow`/`.m`/`.fine` on the web, i.e. the small-caps design system, so caps in the source is redundant with the modifier but is not shouting; (b) `renderClubGroups` returns early on `state.demo` (index.html:10928), so ROOM-6 is on the real path; (c) `openSeasonCeremony` bails on `state.demo` at index.html:13122, so ROOM-4 is real; (d) the web twin of ROOM-8 writes to `#phaseSub`, which sits inside `<div class="title" style="display:none">` (index.html:2963–2965) — the auditor was right that it is live on the phone alone; (e) ROOM-9 has no web twin at all ("FRESH SLATE" and "WHOEVER" return zero hits in index.html). Two findings were materially reworked rather than accepted: ROOM-5's fix (a bare `stageLabel(null,{bare:true})` would silently drop the first-tee date the phone's `phaseHeader` appends, so the replacement has to mirror `LeagueCopy.phaseHeader` rather than call the bare form), and ROOM-14 (the auditor framed "index" as a banned word — it is not; `LeagueCopy.indexSub` and YouSections.swift:86 use it openly. The real defect is narrower: one table, two clients, two column heads. I dropped the auditor's "and the same swap in the three row subs," because ReceiptSheets.swift:57/111 and CupFinalRaceView.swift:103 have exact web twins that also say "vs index" — those are consistent across clients and changing them is a vocabulary decision, not a divergence fix). One thing I found while verifying that is NOT in scope of these findings but is worth a look on the next pass: index.html:12715 and CareerRecord.swift:25 both ship "Cup Season keeps the books — never the money," which reads as a restatement of the RETIRED "tracked, never held" promise on a money surface.

All seven findings survive verification — every quoted string exists at (or within one line of) the cited location, none is demo-gated, dead code, a comment, or a small-caps LABEL. Three corrections to the auditor's reasoning are folded into the findings above: BOARD-1's phrase is on a third live surface it missed (the public share card, index.html:19922); BOARD-5's "founder desk" complaint is wrong on the facts (that term is already spoken to golfers at index.html:15380 and TourCardSheet.swift:137), leaving only the duplicated question, which makes the fix a deletion; BOARD-6's "nobody says it across a cart" argument does not hold, because "on the books" is the money door's own headline — the sharper objection is that the schedule post is borrowing the ledger's phrase, on top of the real defect, which is the full-name/firstname split.

Two things worth the fixer knowing. (1) BOARD-1 and BOARD-4 are one law-break with two heads: "$N on the line" is written independently by the web client, the phone, and the share card, and whichever client taps Finish decides which sentence the league reads. The server fallback at 20260831120000_board_voice_natural_case.sql:911-920 already writes the correct voice ("That's $10.") and is only reached when a client sends no story — so the servers are clean and the clients are the whole problem. Older migrations (20260830280000:238, 20260830260000:163, 20260830220000:275, and earlier) still contain the phrase but are superseded by 20260831120000 and render nothing. (2) LiveEngineTests.swift:131 hard-asserts the exact defective string and must change with BOARD-4.

Not a finding, noted in passing: events.decided_by is stored but never read by either client, so BOARD-2's blast radius is exactly the one completion post — there is no second surface to keep in sync when the wording changes.

DROPPED — DOOR-1 (legal.html:82, \"does not collect, hold, transfer, or distribute money, takes no fee or cut of any prize pool\"). The string is real and at the right line, but the decision it cites rules the other way, in terms: D39 (spec/decision-log.md:1101–1135) says \"legal.html is untouched: it is present-tense fact, accurate today; if a money service ever ships, that is a compliance project (money-transmission territory), not a copy edit.\" D39's own \"Current\" paragraph even quotes this exact sentence as the fact the retired voice line was matching. The retirement covers the product's voice — covenant, wizard help, pot pane, README, GTM — not the disclaimer. Replacing a legal term with brand copy would be relitigating a logged decision, and the proposed FIX also deletes protective language. No finding.

WHAT VERIFICATION MOVED, beyond the drop: DOOR-14's rendered string is worse than filed — Supabase's raw \"Token has expired or is invalid\" clears looksLikeOurSentence's shape gate (index.html:4429) and prints verbatim, so it is a leak, not a shrug, and the fix must keep humanError's network branch rather than replace the call. DOOR-16's proposed rewrite was factually false: both call sites clear cs_code before attempting the join (19658, 19722), so \"the invite is still here\" cannot be promised. DOOR-8's third repetition is at 2831, not 2830. DOOR-14's quote in the source carries the literal escape \\u2019, not a typographic apostrophe. DOOR-18 downgraded law-break → register (D119 is an IA decision about the Home hero; its principle applies, its letter does not) and DOOR-6 downgraded to polish on reachability.

CHECKS THAT CLEARED, so nobody re-runs them: nothing on this list is demo-only — D83 retired the demo door (index.html:17369) and no user path sets state.demo; the covenant, welcome and invite paths are all live. CardGateView:173's capitals are CSEyebrowStyle's textCase(.uppercase) (CSDesign/Sources/CSDesign/Typography.swift:58–68), i.e. the design system, and are NOT reported as shouting — that finding is about a label slot carrying a disclaimer. DoorAppleError.noToken was traced end to end (raise at DoorAppleButton:30 → DoorView:306/313 → AuthRules.human's fall-through at :71) and does reach the door.

ONE THING BEYOND THE DOOR, for whoever owns the ledger line: it is not verbatim anywhere in either client. The correct-noun variants — index.html:19418 and :14246, JoinLeagueFlow.swift:236, BylawsCard.swift:73, GuideCopy.swift:92 — all read \"...keeps the ledger... the money moves between you\" or \"...friend-to-friend\", never \"between friends\". Two more say \"the app keeps the ledger\" (index.html:3546, WizardState.swift:375), which drops the brand name the canon puts in the sentence. The door findings above fix \"tab\" → \"ledger\"; whether the house variant \"between you\" is the line or a drift from it is the owner's call, and it wants one ruling rather than six edits.

surface: POSTING (Post a round composer, hole grid, pars sheet, even-par guard, epilogue) — index.html + apps/ios/CupSeason/Post/**
note:
DROPPED — POST-9, CSPageHeader("Golf", sub: "Play one live, post one you just finished, or plan the next") at apps/ios/CupSeason/Post/PostCoverView.swift:90. The string is exactly as quoted and it does render, but it does not survive question 3. A page header that names the three tenses above three rows that are the three tenses is summary-then-detail, which is how a door orients someone — not the worked example's shape, which was an explanation duplicated between a line and the button under it. The web twin (index.html:3189) is a `.eyebrow` — the design system's section-label slot, per rule 4 — and it is this door's only tagline; deleting it on iOS is a layout decision with a citation attached (the comment at PostCoverView.swift:89 keeps it verbatim from the web for IOS-022 item 4), not a copy defect.

CORRECTIONS TO THE AUDITOR'S LINE NUMBERS: the web's #calcMsg twin in POST-5 is index.html:6930 (not 6931); the web's "Scrap the scan" link in POST-13 is index.html:3395 (not 3413); the even-par fine print's web twin is index.html:7126 (auditor's 7124–7125 covers the openSheet call, the fine print is 7126). Every other quoted line number was exact.

THREE REWRITES REPLACED. POST-2: the auditor wanted the vs chip deleted as duplication; canon §3 licenses exactly that shape ("story first, table second"), and deleting it erases the figure altogether in the middle band, where vsPhrase returns "played to your number" with no number. The defect is the noun — one word. POST-6: deleting "and it posts at half value, half a round" removes the only pre-entry mention of half value; cut the doubling instead. POST-3: "No league yet?" must stay — it is what explains the chip.

THE PATTERN UNDER THE FINDINGS: the pinned bottom bar is where this surface repeats itself. In both empty states it restates the calc panel's instruction (POST-4, POST-5), and its third control restates its own verb (POST-12). The bar has one job — the gross — and it should be silent until it has one. Second pattern: the vocabulary split. "your number" is the crew's word everywhere the app tells a story (CSBands, RoundCopy, GuideCopy, the web's own #calcVs label) and "your index" survives only in the places engineered earliest — the band table and the vs chip on the composer, plus the screen eyebrow at PostRoundModel.swift:65 ("Post a round · your index 12.4"), which I did NOT report: that one names the golfer's real WHS handicap index as a standalone figure, which is the golfer's own word for it, not a band comparison.

One thing that is right and worth not breaking: PostHeroContent's "A preview — your league's own math scores it on the books." (PostRoundScreen.swift:407) is D178 doing its job and is not redundant with anything on the card.

surface: YOU (iOS) — You tab, Tour Card, rivalry sheet, and the Card & settings drawer behind the ⚙
note:
Sixteen of the seventeen findings verify; one (YOU-16, the Major clause in the guide) is dropped. Nothing here is demo-only, dead code, or a comment: every string I kept is rendered by a live view I traced to its call site.

Line-number corrections the auditor got wrong: YOU-14's two pairs are YouHero.swift:91 (hint) / :94 (visible) and CredentialCard.swift:112 (hint) / :125 (visible), not :67/:70 and :71/:84. Every other line number was accurate.

DROPPED — YOU-16 (GuideCopy.swift:46, the Major clause). The string and the flag both check out: `EventFlags.majorEnabled()` fails closed (EventFlags.swift:16–20) and EventPickerSheet.swift:28 hides the row on it. But this is a flag/copy sync question, not a copy defect traceable to any of the named laws — the file's own header calls the flag "the v1 curtain, not a delete", the Major ships in the binary, and a golfer can be in a Major started elsewhere. The proposed fix is also a code change, not a copy change. Worth a product decision; not a voice finding.

Adjacent instances of the SAME defects that the auditor did not list, all one command away, for whoever writes the fix:
- apps/ios/CupSeason/You/TourCardSheet.swift:93 — `MathRow(label: "Avg vs index", value: c.avgText)` sits one line under YOU-4's "Best diff": the same D1 drift as YOU-17, in the same block.
- apps/ios/CupSeason/You/YouSections.swift:129 — the recent-round VoiceOver label ends `…gross, differential \(SliceFormat.raw(r.differential))`. Spoken to a golfer, so it is a user surface, and it says the banned word outright.

- apps/ios/Packages/CupSeasonKit/Sources/CupSeasonKit/You/Rivalries.swift:86 — `sheetSub` reads "WEEKLY CLASH · BETTER ROUND VS INDEX TAKES THE WEEK"; keeping it is right (YOU-10 keeps it), but it inherits the same "index" vs "your number" question if D1 is applied consistently.

Cross-client: fifteen of the sixteen have a verbatim web twin in index.html (I checked each — e.g. the mute label at 15283, "THIS IS HOW YOUR BUDDIES SEE YOU" at 15313, the money note at 12715, "Diff " at 12629). The two exceptions are YOU-3 and YOU-17, where the WEB is already better — index.html:3108 says "Best vs index" and :3109 says "Avg vs your number / across counting rounds", so the phone drifted on its own. Every other fix should land on both clients or the two will disagree.

One thing this surface gets right and should not be touched: the empty states and error states on the Tour Card ("Could not pull the card — check your signal and try again.", TourCard.privateLine, "Pulling the weeks…") are D160 to the letter — they say what happened to you, never what the system did.

surface: Push — the notification generators (SQL + edge function) and the friend-request email
note: Verified all seven. Five survive, two are dropped. DROPPED — PUSH-4 (supabase/migrations/20260901120000_the_takedown_path.sql:334-335). The string exists exactly as quoted and is the live definition (trg_report_wakes_founder, newest migration). But the recipient is `founder_id()` — one person, the owner, and only when someone reports content. It is an internal moderation ping, not golfer-facing copy. Worse for the finding: the auditor's own routing note argues against the fix. The payload is `{report_id, desk}`, neither key is in CS_ID_KEYS (supabase/functions/push/index.ts:103-106), so the tap lands Home. "Open the founder's desk" is not a narration of the control — it is the only wayfinding the recipient gets, because the tap cannot get there. Cutting it makes the notification worse until the router is fixed. Worth handing the routing observation to whoever owns push routing; it is not a copy finding. DROPPED — PUSH-6 (supabase/migrations/20260828040000_nudge_payloads.sql:145-152). String verified, live definition (newest of two `round_duel_nudge` defs). But the claim that this push "inverts" the house shape is wrong: `split()` (index.ts:74-84) only ever touches board posts. Every personal `push_nudges` row carries a generator-authored title and body verbatim, and the convention for those is stated in the code itself — 20260827210000_push_wave7.sql:74, "Title = the container's name (what the lock screen bolds)". This push follows it. The render is "August Ryder / Marcus Webb posted — +2.3 to beat · closes tonight": the container bold, the number-story underneath, already spoken as story with the named band ("to beat", not "differential"). That is the law being obeyed, not broken. One small true thing that is not worth a finding on its own: this generator uses the full `display_name` (line 145) where the tee-sheet-voice generators use `split_part(..., ' ', 1)`, so it says "Marcus Webb posted" where the rest of push says "Marcus". Fold it into whatever pass touches this function next. Corroboration found for PUSH-1 while checking: the web client already words the same fact without the accusation — index.html:14064, "Still to post: names · closes tonight." The iOS reminder is the only place in the product that turns that into "You haven't posted." In good voice and left alone: the friend-request email body (index.ts:367-369) — "Rick wants in your crew on Cup Season." / "Accept and their rounds land in your feed, all season." News, then what it gets you, no urgency. The lock-screen action words (PushPayload.swift:143-145: "I'm in" / "Can't") are the crew's own voice, not UI-speak.

surface: EMAIL — supabase/functions/season-email/index.ts (season recap + league cancellation), supabase/functions/push/index.ts (friend-request mail), index.html:19780–19803 (the ?unsub= takeover)
note:
All eight audited findings survived verification: every string exists at the quoted line (quotes corrected for encoding on 122/176 and 19798), none is demo-only, none is dead code, none is a small-caps LABEL mistaken for shouting. I split the two "Whoever collected it" twins into separate rows (EMAIL-4 / EMAIL-4B) because they are two physical edits in two different mails.

Things that are RIGHT on this surface and should not be touched: the recap mail's CTA "See the rounds behind it" (season-email:120) is the house standard for a control — fairway, and it names the tap; the subject line "The Cup goes to ${champ} by ${gap} — ${league}" is story-first and works for a squad or a solo champion; the cancellation subject "${league} is off — your $50 comes back" answers the money question in the subject; "Your rounds stay on your card — all of them" (:174) is the right reassurance at the right size; the D77 copy notes are kept OUT of the templates so no HTML comment ships. The named-band law holds throughout — no PvI, differential, month_rank or index_at_post reaches any of these mails; the season table speaks points and names only.

One thing outside this surface that a fixer should know before touching EMAIL-1/EMAIL-2: the same non-canonical ledger wording lives in five more user-facing places and will read inconsistent if only the emails are fixed — index.html:3546, 3780, 12715, 13148, and iOS SeasonCeremonyView.swift:63 ("Cup Season keeps the books. Money moves friend-to-friend — we just make sure nobody argues at the bar."). Only the two email lines carry "never through us", which is the D39 violation proper; the rest are wording drift. index.html:19418 and iOS BylawsCard.swift:73 / JoinLeagueFlow.swift:236 already speak the canon line correctly and are the model.

Verified all 27 against source. 21 survive; 6 dropped, with reasons a fixer needs:

DROPPED — ERR-6 (index.html:19766) and ERR-5 (19765): both halves of one ternary inside the hash-error IIFE at 19762–19772. The string quotes and lines are exact, but the branch can only fire when Supabase puts `error=` in the URL hash, which only redirect flows produce. This client has no `emailRedirectTo` (comment at index.html:16139) and no `signInWithOAuth` anywhere — grep returns zero hits for both. Nothing the product sends can land a golfer on that branch. The link-vocabulary copy is genuinely wrong for a code-only product and is worth one line if someone is in the file, but it is not a defect a golfer meets.

DROPPED — ERR-15 (index.html:17700 and its iOS twin FeedbackSheet.swift:189): the founder's desk. index.html:3052–3053 says it in the markup: "the founder's desk: hidden for everyone but the owner; the SERVER is the gate (founder_desk/founder_note refuse non-founders)". "push the founder_desk migration" is read by exactly one person, and it is the one person who can push it. Not a golfer surface.

DROPPED — ERR-17 (index.html:16057): the whole branch is behind `nativePush()` (16008), which returns null unless `window.Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` is true. CLAUDE.md:278: "`apps/mobile/` (Expo B1) and `ios-wrapper/` are retired by D99." No Capacitor shell ships, so no golfer can reach the APNs branch. The web-push branch below it is live — that one is ERR-23, and it survives.

DROPPED — ERR-26 (index.html:10546): `navigator.clipboard?.writeText(...)` at 10545 is NOT awaited, so a clipboard rejection is an unhandled promise, not a caught throw. The catch cannot fire; "Copy failed" is unreachable. (Worth handing to engineering separately: because the write is unawaited, 10545 toasts "Recap link copied" even when the copy fails. The sibling at 10587 awaits correctly.)

CORRECTED — ERR-27's reasoning was wrong and its rewrite would have shipped a bug: 7401 is the `#postPhotoFile` handler (attaching a photo to a round), not the scan path. "type your nines in" is nonsense advice there. Kept with a corrected rewrite.

TWO FINDINGS ARE ROOT CAUSES, and roughly half the rest are downstream of them. ERR-1 (AuthRules.swift:71 + SupabaseService.swift:26) is the big one: `SupabaseService.describe` (:154) joins `[e.code, e.message]`, so a PostgREST failure is already "P0001 Not enough golfers…" before `RpcError.errorDescription` (:26) glues the RPC's function name to the front. Every iOS toast that ends in `AuthRules.human` or `roomError` (RoomBits.swift:259) shows both. Fix that one line and ERR-10, ERR-24 and the iOS half of ERR-9 (CardAndSettingsScreen.swift:133) all get quieter. ERR-2 is the same story on the board mapper. Three error mappers ship on iOS — AuthRules.human, BoardText.humanError (BoardText.swift:107), HumanError.text (PeopleModels.swift) — against the web's one; that is the structural finding under all of these.

The good news, said plainly: the web's `humanError` (index.html:4393) and `looksLikeOurSentence` (4427) are excellent, and the Q-08 allowlist inside it is exactly right. Almost every web error that routes through `humanError` is in voice. The defects below are the paths that skip it (15662, 19689, 19618, 17342) or that add words after it (17244).

Verification notes for the reader. (1) The iOS app ships NO demo/diorama — `grep -rl "diorama|isDemo|demoLeague" apps/ios/CupSeason apps/ios/Packages/.../Sources` returns nothing — so rule 3 never applied; every finding below renders to a real golfer, and I confirmed a live caller for each string. (2) All 26 submitted findings existed at or within a line of the quoted location; I corrected no line numbers, but I rewrote several fixes and re-anchored three rationales. (3) I dropped the ALL-CAPS half of the Cup Final finding: `PhaseHero`'s `m:` slot is `CSFont.label` + tracking (RoomBits.swift:139), i.e. the small-caps LABEL slot, and every sibling value (kickoff, seatFill) is authored in caps — that is the design system, not shouting. Only the standings-empty pair survives the caps test, because it is two fully punctuated sentences, em dash and terminal periods included. (4) The big cross-client fact: most of the math-jargon strings have exact twins in index.html (`DIFF `, `Diff `, the "Beat your index by 3+" band table at 3446–3452, "vs your index" in the Ryder rule at 13997, "Squad formation"/"Unlocks when settings lock" at 3657, "never the money" at 12715, "nobody argues at the bar" at 13149), so those are shipped-canon breaches on BOTH clients, not phone drift — the fix has to land twice. The genuinely phone-only regressions are the Home `easeCaps` (the web has one shared `easeCaps` at index.html:5169), the claim-door button, "A preview — your league's own math…", `golfer(s)`, "Everything locks at the first tee", "FRESH SLATE", and the four You-screen labels where the web already says "your number". (5) In good voice and worth protecting: GuideCopy.swift:79–83 and JoinLeagueFlow.swift:224–228 (the band names, done right twice), CSBands/RoundCopy's `pointsFor` lines, LeagueCopy's `nextUp` month text, and the whole `*Copy.swift` factoring — note that nearly every defect below lives in an INLINE string in a view file (StandingsPane, YouSections, IndividualRaceView, TourCardSheet, the two setup sheets), which is exactly where the copy discipline stops.

All 14 findings survived verification; none were dropped. Corrections made: STORE-8's quote begins at docs/ios/app-store-listing.md:83, not :84 (it wraps 83-85) — every other line number and quote was exact as filed. Nothing on this surface is demo-gated, dead, a code comment, or a small-caps label; legal.html is the live page behind the Privacy Policy URL (docs/ios/app-store-listing.md:110 confirms it is the same link the sign-in screen and Settings use), and the .md files hold the literal text destined for App Store Connect fields.

Two things worth saying that are not findings. First, the money paragraph in the listing itself (docs/ios/app-store-listing.md:87-90) is the one place on this surface that gets the ledger law exactly right — canon verbatim, "every dollar of your crew's pot on the books", and "A league can also run on bragging rights alone" as the out. It is the model the other three documents should be edited toward, and STORE-2 and STORE-14 are both just "do what line 87 already does." Second, the defects cluster by document age rather than by author: legal.html is stamped "Last updated: July 18, 2026" (lines 50 and 69), two days before D39 landed (brand-canon.md:64, "amended 2026-07-20"), and every one of the six legal.html findings is a pre-D39 sentence that simply never got the pass. The launch kit is dated 2026-07-20 (line 3) and its two findings are both places where docs/ios/ later overtook it. A single dated re-pass on legal.html would close six of fourteen.

One pattern the filed findings only touch obliquely: the whole "prize pool" section (legal.html:78-83) is written in a defensive register that belongs to no one — "not a game of chance", "applicable laws where they play" — until the last clause, which is suddenly in voice: "keep your league to bragging rights" (line 83). That clause is what the section should sound like throughout, and it is already the listing's own closer at line 90.
